ref_extractions.title: Age and sex modulate the variability of neural responses to naturalistic videos
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: Paper uses HBN EEG data to study age/sex effects on neural variability via inter-subject correlation during naturalistic video watching. While it uses HBN EEG data, the analysis focuses on neural variability rather than a concrete supervised ML classification/regression task with defined labels.
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Uses HBN EEG data but does not define a supervised ML task
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: N=114 initial + N=303 replication cohort from HBN; examines inter-subject correlation of evoked EEG responses to classroom and Hollywood video clips

ref_extractions.title: HBN-EEG: The FAIR implementation of the Healthy Brain Network (HBN) electroencephalography dataset
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is THE primary descriptor paper for the HBN-EEG dataset, explicitly describing the six-task paradigm (Resting State, Surround Suppression, Movie Watching, Sequence Learning, Contrast Change Detection, Symbol Search) and dataset releases on OpenNeuro. While it focuses on data description rather than a specific ML application, it is the foundational paper for this dataset.
ref_extractions.epoch_params: Six tasks: resting state, surround suppression, movie watching, sequence learning, contrast detection, symbol search; active tasks involve button press responses
ref_extractions.label_mapping: Labels include internalizing, externalizing, attention, p-factor dimensions from bifactor model
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Describes dataset creation; available psychopathology dimensions (internalizing, externalizing, attention, p-factor) enable super-level classification tasks
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: 2639+ participants across 9 releases; 128-channel EEG; HED-annotated events; describes both passive (no response) and active (mouse click response) tasks

ref_extractions.title: An open resource for transdiagnostic research in pediatric mental health and learning disorders
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper describes the overall HBN Biobank initiative including MRI, genetics, and other modalities. While it mentions EEG as part of the biobank, it does not specifically describe or use the EEG dataset (ds005515).
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Describes HBN Biobank design; not specific to EEG dataset
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Initial release n=664; covers fMRI, diffusion MRI, EEG, eye-tracking, voice/video, genetics, actigraphy

ref_extractions.title: A resource for assessing information processing in the developing brain using EEG and eye tracking
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is the original pilot dataset paper for the HBN EEG protocol (126 individuals, ages 6-44) that preceded the larger HBN-EEG releases. It describes the six-task paradigm that is the foundation of ds005515. However, it describes the initial small-scale release (sdata.2017.40) rather than the current large-scale OpenNeuro release.
ref_extractions.paradigm: six-task battery (contrast detection, sequence learning, symbol search, resting, surround suppression, videos)
ref_extractions.epoch_params: Three active tasks (contrast detection, sequence learning, symbol search) and three passive tasks (resting, surround suppression, videos)
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Describes pilot dataset (n=126) that evolved into HBN-EEG (n=2600+); paradigm details align with ds005515 but different release
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: 126 subjects, ages 6-44; 80.2% typically developing, 19.8% clinical disorders; same six-task paradigm as full HBN-EEG

ref_extractions.title: HBN-EEG: The FAIR implementation of the Healthy Brain Network (HBN) electroencephalography dataset
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: Full PDF version of the HBN-EEG descriptor paper. Provides detailed methodology for the dataset including six tasks, event annotations using HED tags, and data quality checks. This is the primary reference for ds005515.
ref_extractions.epoch_params: tmin/tmax vary by task; active tasks: contrast detection, sequence learning, symbol search; passive tasks: resting state, surround suppression, movie watching
ref_extractions.label_mapping: internalizing, externalizing, attention, p-factor (bifactor model psychopathology dimensions)
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Super-level labels available; enables multi-label classification of psychiatric dimensions
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: 2639 participants across 9 releases; BIDS formatted; HED annotations; quality checks performed; includes behavioral and participant response data

ref_extractions.title: Towards clinical applications of movie fMRI
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper discusses movie fMRI methodology and clinical applications. It does not use the HBN-EEG dataset or any EEG data. While related to naturalistic stimuli research, it is not relevant to ds005515.

ref_extractions.title: Functional connectivity of EEG is subject-specific, associated with phenotype, and different from fMRI
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: Paper explicitly uses HBN Biobank EEG data (N=1657 children/adolescents) to analyze EEG functional connectivity via phase-coupling. It examines brain-behavior relationships with phenotypes including age, sex, IQ, ADHD, and socioeconomic status. While primarily an association study, it demonstrates ML-ready analysis of this dataset.
ref_extractions.epoch_params: Continuous resting and video segments; phase-coupling (imaginary coherence) computed across frequency bands
ref_extractions.label_mapping: Phenotypic measures: age, sex, IQ, ADHD, anxiety, socioeconomic status, Child Behavior Checklist Score
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Association study showing phenotype prediction capability; demonstrates EEG FC predicts individual differences
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: 1657 individuals from HBN Biobank; resting state and video conditions; frequency bands alpha, theta, beta, gamma; connectivity-phenotype correlation analysis

ref_extractions.title: A benchmark for prediction of psychiatric multimorbidity from resting EEG data in a large pediatric sample
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper defines explicit ML benchmark challenges using HBN resting EEG data (N=2042). Challenge 1 is multi-task multi-label classification of 7 DSM-V psychiatric diagnoses. Challenge 2 is multiple regression for symptom severity. This is the most concrete ML task definition for the HBN-EEG dataset in the reference set.
ref_extractions.epoch_params: Resting state EEG segments; features from power spectral density, phase coupling, or other EEG metrics
ref_extractions.label_mapping: 7 DSM-V diagnoses (multi-label): ADHD, ODD, ASD, anxiety disorder, mood disorder, PTSD, psychotic symptoms; plus dimensional severity scores
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Explicitly defines multi-label classification and regression benchmarks; 56%+ of children have psychiatric multimorbidity
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: N=2042 from HBN; resting state EEG only plus demographics; hidden test sets provided; community challenge format

ref_extractions.title: The Coronavirus Health and Impact Survey (CRISIS) reveals reproducible correlates of pandemic-related mood states across the Atlantic
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper describes the CRISIS survey for pandemic mental health research. It does not use EEG data or the HBN-EEG dataset. While one author (Michael Milham) is affiliated with HBN, this study uses survey data from Prolific, not neuroimaging data.

ref_extractions.evidence_desc: N=5646 from Prolific; survey instrument for COVID mental health impacts; no EEG component

feasibility_reason: The HBN EEG dataset has well-defined event structures (left/right targets, button presses, resting/video/contrast trial blocks) that support multiple ML tasks including contrast detection classification and resting-state vs task classification, supported by relevant references documenting the multi-task battery paradigm.
tasks_section:
## Tasks

### Classical Task 1: Psychiatric Multimorbidity Classification from Resting EEG (Super-meta)
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_segmentation_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: segment_length = 4.0 s, overlap = 0.0, target_events = [`resting_start`]
- **Label Route**: `info`
- **Meta Level**: super
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|--------|
  | N/A | 0–6 (multi-label) | ADHD, ODD, ASD, anxiety disorder, mood disorder, PTSD, psychotic symptoms |
- **Evidence**:
  - DOI: 10.1016/j.neuroimage.2022.119348 — Benchmark for prediction of psychiatric multimorbidity from resting EEG; N=2042; 7 DSM-V diagnoses; community challenge format with hidden test sets
- **Kernel Notes**: Kernel must join EEG subject IDs with phenotypic CSV containing DSM-V diagnosis fields. Multi-label setup (binary per diagnosis) rather than single-label; exclude subjects missing all diagnosis labels. Admin markers (`boundary`, `9999`) excluded from segmentation.

### Classical Task 2: Phenotypic Regression from EEG Connectivity (Super-meta)
- **Task Type**: regression
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_long_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = 0.0 s, tmax = 2.0 s, overlap = 0.0, target_events = [`resting_start`, `video_start`]
- **Label Route**: `misc`
- **Meta Level**: super
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|--------|
  | N/A | continuous | Age, IQ, ADHD-SWAN, CBCL, SCARED anxiety, Barratt SES |
- **Evidence**:
  - DOI: 10.1016/j.neuroimage.2020.117001 — Functional connectivity predicts phenotype; N=1657; connectivity (imaginary coherence) across alpha/theta/beta/gamma bands correlates with age, sex, IQ, ADHD, anxiety, SES, CBCL scores
  - DOI: 10.1101/2024.10.03.615261 — HBN-EEG FAIR implementation; describes internalizing, externalizing, attention, p-factor dimensions available as super-level labels
- **Kernel Notes**: Kernel must compute connectivity features (phase coupling) before regression. Use resting state segments for primary analysis; video segments as secondary condition. MISC labels (`response_time`) available but phenotypic variables require join with subject metadata CSV.

### Classical Task 3: Contrast Detection Stimulus Classification (Raw-meta)
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.5 s, tmax = 1.0 s, target_events = [`left_target`, `right_target`]
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|--------|
  | `left_target` | 0 | Left-tilted stimulus onset (contrast change) |
  | `right_target` | 1 | Right-tilted stimulus onset (contrast change) |
- **Evidence**:
  - DOI: 10.1038/sdata.2017.40 — Pilot HBN dataset (n=126) establishing six-task paradigm including contrast detection; active task with button press responses
  - DOI: 10.1101/2024.10.03.615261 — HBN-EEG release describes contrast detection as active task with stimulus-locked epochs
- **Kernel Notes**: Exclude admin markers (`boundary`, `9999`). Fixation point (`fixpoint_ON`) precedes targets as trial cue. May extend to stimulus-response accuracy by matching button presses to preceding targets.

### Normal Task 1: Resting-State EEG vs. Active Task State Classification (Raw-meta)
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = 0.0 s, tmax = 2.0 s, target_events = [`resting_start`, `contrastTrial_start`, `seqLearning_start`, `symbolSearch_start`]
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|--------|
  | `resting_start` | 0 | Resting-state block onset |
  | `contrastTrial_start` | 1 | Contrast detection trial block onset |
  | `seqLearning_start` | 2 | Sequence learning block onset |
  | `symbolSearch_start` | 3 | Symbol search block onset |
- **Evidence**:
  - DOI: 10.1101/2024.10.03.615261 — Multi-task battery description; resting, passive, and active task conditions are distinguishable paradigm types
  - DOI: 10.1038/sdata.2017.40 — Three active and three passive tasks described; active tasks require button press responses
- **Kernel Notes**: 4-class classification of brain state from block-onset epochs. Video watching excluded from primary task due to longer sustained processing. Eye-instruction events (`instructed_toOpenEyes`, `instructed_toCloseEyes`) may enable eyes-open vs eyes-closed sub-classification within resting.

### Potential Task 1: Sequence Learning Paradigm Classification (Raw-meta)
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_long_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = 0.0 s, tmax = 4.0 s, overlap = 0.0, target_events = [`seqLearning_start`, `seqLearning_stop`, `learningBlock_1`, `learningBlock_2`, `learningBlock_3`, `learningBlock_4`]
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|--------|
  | `seqLearning_start` | 0 | Sequence learning block onset |
  | `seqLearning_stop` | 1 | Sequence learning block offset |
- **Evidence**:
  - DOI: 10.1101/2024.10.03.615261 — Describes sequence learning as active task in HBN battery
  - DOI: 10.1038/sdata.2017.40 — Sequence learning described in six-task paradigm
- **Kernel Notes**: Limited event counts (seqLearning_start: 18, seqLearning_stop: 9) may restrict sample size. Aggregate across learningBlock markers to increase trials if individual block counts insufficient.

### Potential Task 2: Symbol Search Cognitive Task Classification (Raw-meta)
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.5 s, tmax = 1.0 s, target_events = [`symbolSearch_start`]
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|--------|
  | `symbolSearch_start` | 0 | Symbol search trial block onset |
- **Evidence**:
  - DOI: 10.1101/2024.10.03.615261 — Symbol search listed as active task requiring cognitive processing
  - DOI: 10.1038/sdata.2017.40 — Symbol search in six-task battery
- **Kernel Notes**: Single condition (no binary classification) limits discriminative analysis. Consider regression on response time or trial accuracy if behavioral data available. Limited events (70) may restrict model training.

### Potential Task 3: Surround Suppression Paradigm Analysis (Raw-meta)
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.5 s, tmax = 1.0 s, target_events = [`surroundSuppB1_start`, `surroundSuppB2_start`]
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|--------|
  | `surroundSuppB1_start` | 0 | Surround suppression block 1 onset |
  | `surroundSuppB2_start` | 1 | Surround suppression block 2 onset |
- **Evidence**:
  - DOI: 10.1038/sdata.2017.40 — Surround suppression listed as passive task in six-task paradigm
- **Kernel Notes**: Sub-block markers with limited counts (B1: 98, B2: 67). May need to aggregate or use parent-level event if available. Passive task—no motor response required.
